claims.claim: Direct Tokunbo Valeo Alternator for Mercedes-Benz M278 - 439741
claims.evidence: Photos show an alternator but no clearly readable brand/model/part number (e.g., Valeo logo or '439741') to confirm the exact application.
No paperwork/labels visible in the photos that confirm origin.

claims.claim: Tested and working, no knock, low mileage, never opened.
claims.evidence: Photos cannot confirm electrical testing, internal bearing noise ('no knock'), mileage, or whether it has been opened.

risks.risk: Wrong alternator fitment/application (M278) or wrong part number; connectors/voltage/current rating may differ.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the alternator label/part number (including Valeo/Bosch and the exact reference) plus a photo of the connector side showing pin/plug type.
risks.if_unproven: Price it as a generic used Mercedes alternator with unknown fitment and unknown electrical condition (worst case: not guaranteed to work).

risks.risk: Not actually tested/working; possible diode/regulator failure or weak output that won’t show in photos.
risks.proof: Video or screenshot of bench test results (output voltage/current) or an on-car test (charging voltage at idle and at 2,000–3,000 rpm).
risks.if_unproven: Price it as not working/needs testing or repair.

risks.risk: Bearing noise ('no knock') or pulley/freewheel issues not visible externally.
risks.proof: Clip showing the pulley spun by hand and a short sound check (or a short on-car running video showing no abnormal noise).
risks.if_unproven: Price it as having potential bearing/pulley wear (worst case: may require replacement).

risks.risk: Condition of electrical terminals/connectors and internal windings may be worse than it looks (corrosion, heat damage).
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the regulator/terminal area and the connector contacts; plus a photo of any date/serial label.
risks.if_unproven: Price it as used with possible corrosion/heat damage (worst case: reduced reliability).

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the alternator nameplate/label showing brand (Valeo/Bosch) and the exact part number (including '439741' if that’s on the label).
Photo of the full connector/terminal side with the plug type clearly visible.
Proof of testing: charging voltage readings (idle and revs) or bench test results (voltage/current).
Video of pulley spin + short running sound check.
response.reason: The photos confirm it is an alternator, but the key identifiers (Valeo branding and the exact part number/application) and the seller’s 'tested/working' claims cannot be verified from the images. Without the label and test proof, a worst-case price would be too speculative.
